hero-widget.description: Manage your portfolio through real historical crises. See if you can beat inflation and preserve capital!

descriptions.gfc_2008: It is Q4 2007. The global economy has been growing steadily for years, and stock markets are reaching all-time highs. You have 10,000 SC in cash and zero investments. The media carries the first troubling reports of 'subprime mortgage loans' in the US, but most analysts downplay the risk. Decide where to allocate your capital!
descriptions.covid_2020: It is January 2020. Financial markets are climbing, and tech companies are breaking records. The first news of a new virus in China begins to emerge. You start this stage with 10,000 SC in pure cash. Choose how to distribute your capital at the start!
descriptions.inflation_2022: It is January 2022. Prices in stores are skyrocketing, and central banks announce the end of the free-money era. You start with 10,000 SC in cash. Your goal is to defend real purchasing power during one of the most challenging years for financial markets!

quarter-news.world-events-title: What was happening in the world:

2007-Q4.headline: First Cracks: Bankruptcies of Smaller Mortgage Funds
2007-Q4.context: In August 2007, BNP Paribas freezes investment funds citing the US subprime crisis. In the UK, a run on Northern Rock sees customers line up to withdraw cash. Central banks pump billions into liquidity as initial panic grips global markets.
2007-Q4.lesson: Gold and bonds immediately react to the first signs of uncertainty in the banking sector.

2008-Q1.headline: March 2008: Collapse and Fire Sale of Bear Stearns
2008-Q1.context: The fifth-largest Wall Street investment bank teeters on bankruptcy and is acquired by JPMorgan with government backing.
2008-Q1.lesson: Financial sector risks spread wider, stocks deepen losses, and capital flees to safe-haven bonds.

2008-Q2.headline: Brief Stabilization and Mounting Inflationary Pressure
2008-Q2.context: Crude oil prices set an all-time high ($140 per barrel), driving inflation while the broader economy decelerates sharply.
2008-Q2.lesson: Stagflation (high inflation + economic slowdown) restricts central banks from quickly bailing out markets.

2008-Q3.headline: September 2008: Lehman Brothers Collapse and Liquidity Freeze
2008-Q3.context: On September 15, 2008, 158-year-old Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy. Global banks freeze lending. Equities plummet.
2008-Q3.lesson: Lacking a liquidity buffer and panic-selling during this shock is the single most common novice mistake.

2008-Q4.headline: Peak Panic: Worst Quarter for Stocks Since the 1930s
2008-Q4.context: Equities dive -21.9% in just three months. US Treasuries skyrocket by a record +14.8% as the ultimate safe harbor.
2008-Q4.lesson: This quarter proved the power of government bonds – investors holding 40% bonds limited their loss from -22% down to only -7%.

2009-Q1.headline: March 9, 2009: Historic Market Bottom and Peak Despair
2009-Q1.context: The S&P 500 hits a generational low at 666 points. Headlines trumpet the end of capitalism. Right then, the longest bull market in history is born.
2009-Q1.lesson: Holding or accumulating quality assets when everyone else panics (Buffett: 'Be greedy when others are fearful') delivers supreme long-term wealth.

2009-Q2.headline: Bailout Packages Unleashed and Fierce Rebound (+15.9%)
2009-Q2.context: Governments roll out TARP and the Federal Reserve begins quantitative easing (QE). Stock markets rebound violently.
2009-Q2.lesson: Anyone who liquidated everything into cash in March 2009 permanently missed this historic recovery rally.

2009-Q3.headline: Bull Market Continues and Gold Surges (+8.5%)
2009-Q3.context: The macroeconomy gradually heals and investors regain confidence in tech and industrial firms.
2009-Q3.lesson: Diversification allows you to benefit from simultaneous expansions in equities and commodities.

2009-Q4.headline: Confidence Restored and a Winning Finish to 2009
2009-Q4.context: 2009 concludes with a spectacular gain of over 26% for equities for the year, despite kicking off in outright panic.
2009-Q4.lesson: Patience and steadfast allocation discipline beat market timing attempts every single time.

2010-Q1.headline: Solid Start to the New Decade
2010-Q1.context: Corporate balance sheets and quarterly earnings demonstrate robust health as the economic recovery gathers tangible momentum.
2010-Q1.lesson: The economy systematically adapts to new paradigms over time.

2010-Q2.headline: May 2010: Flash Crash and the Greek Debt Crisis
2010-Q2.context: An algorithmic flash crash coupled with Greek sovereign default fears triggers a sharp correction. Gold rallies +11.7%.
2010-Q2.lesson: 10-15% pullbacks are routine features of every healthy bull market and do not imply an impending systemic crash.

2010-Q3.headline: Federal Reserve Signals QE2
2010-Q3.context: Central banks commit to low borrowing costs, reigniting risk appetite in equities and commodities alike.
2010-Q3.lesson: Monetary policy liquidity conditions exert immense direct influence on capital asset prices.

2010-Q4.headline: Strong Year-End Rally Across World Markets
2010-Q4.context: Corporate profitability officially climbs back to pre-2008 peak levels.
2010-Q4.lesson: Investing in the global market is fundamentally a bet on human ingenuity and corporate resilience.

2011-Q1.headline: Fukushima Disaster and Arab Spring Turmoil
2011-Q1.context: Despite severe geopolitical and humanitarian shocks, financial markets remain resilient, backed by strong manufacturing activity.
2011-Q1.lesson: Isolated exogenous events seldom derail secular multi-year economic growth trajectories.

2011-Q2.headline: Economic Cooldown and Eurozone Debt Escalation
2011-Q2.context: Investors closely watch surging bond yields in Italy and Spain as fiscal strains mount across Europe.
2011-Q2.lesson: Short-term volatility is the unavoidable entry price for superior long-term compounded returns.

2011-Q3.headline: August 2011: S&P Downgrades US Credit Rating
2011-Q3.context: For the first time in history, S&P downgrades the US sovereign debt rating from AAA to AA+. Stocks plunge -13.9%, while bonds (+12.9%) and gold protect portfolios.
2011-Q3.lesson: Further proof of the negative correlation between stocks and bonds during flight-to-safety episodes.

2011-Q4.headline: End of the 4-Year Trial by Fire: Market Emerges Victorious
2011-Q4.context: The ECB steps in aggressively, and world markets cap 2011 with a powerful year-end rally, drawing this crisis cycle to a close.
2011-Q4.lesson: You survived the most severe financial crisis since 1929. Review your simulation debrief!

2020-Q1.headline: March 2020: Global Lockdown and Flash Crash (-19.6%)
2020-Q1.context: The WHO declares a global pandemic. Markets experience the fastest 30% drop in modern history. Treasuries climb +8.2% and gold adds +3.9%.
2020-Q1.lesson: During liquidity shocks, investors temporarily sell everything, but defensive quality assets rapidly cushion capital.

2020-Q2.headline: Trillions from Central Banks and Remote Work Boom (+20.5%)
2020-Q2.context: Interest rates drop to zero, governments issue stimulus checks, and Big Tech (Zoom, Amazon, Microsoft) reports record earnings.
2020-Q2.lesson: Liquidating at the bottom in March locked out investors from this historic surge.

2020-Q3.headline: Economic Reopening and Summer Bull Run
2020-Q3.context: Factories resume output, consumer confidence climbs, and gold shatters records by crossing $2,000/oz (over 1,700 €/oz).
2020-Q3.lesson: Equity markets anticipate real economic conditions 6 to 12 months ahead.

2020-Q4.headline: November 2020: Pfizer & BioNTech Vaccine Breakthrough
2020-Q4.context: Confirmation of over 90% vaccine efficacy triggers euphoria. Value and cyclicals ignite into a broad rally.
2020-Q4.lesson: Scientific and technological breakthroughs can completely reverse market sentiment in just hours.

2021-Q1.headline: Rotation into Value Sectors and Rising Bond Yields
2021-Q1.context: Vaccine rollouts accelerate worldwide. Anticipation of economic overheating depresses fixed-rate long-term bonds (-5.7%).
2021-Q1.lesson: When markets expect strong growth and rising yields, prices of existing fixed-rate bonds drop.

2021-Q2.headline: Early Signs of Resurging Inflation (+2.3% in One Quarter)
2021-Q2.context: Snarled supply chains, chip shortages, and pent-up consumer demand drive commodity and producer prices higher.
2021-Q2.lesson: Companies with pricing power pass elevated input costs directly on to customers.

2021-Q3.headline: Summer Pause and the 'Transitory Inflation' Debate
2021-Q3.context: Central banks insist inflation is strictly transitory while major indices consolidate sideways.
2021-Q3.lesson: Sideways consolidations are ideal opportunities to re-evaluate and rebalance portfolio allocations.

2021-Q4.headline: Pandemic Bull Market Finale: S&P 500 Closes Near Record Highs
2021-Q4.context: Despite rising inflation concerns, 2021 closes with double-digit returns for the global stock market.
2021-Q4.lesson: Two years after the global pandemic hit, a disciplined diversified investor gained more than 30%.

2022-Q1.headline: February 2022: Russian Invasion of Ukraine and Commodity Shock
2022-Q1.context: War in Europe sparks a dramatic surge in oil, natural gas, and wheat. Gold surges +5.9% while stocks and bonds tumble.
2022-Q1.lesson: Gold once again affirms its role as an essential geopolitical crisis hedge.

2022-Q2.headline: Aggressive Fed Rate Hikes (+75 bps) and the 60/40 Meltdown
2022-Q2.context: Inflation exceeds 9% in the US and 15% in Poland. Central banks hike aggressively. Unusually, stocks drop -16.1% and bonds drop -5.1%.
2022-Q2.lesson: Rapid rate spikes penalize existing fixed-coupon bonds (interest rate duration risk).

2022-Q3.headline: Peak Bearish Sentiment and the Dollar Sucking Up Liquidity
2022-Q3.context: The US Dollar index reaches multi-decade highs, draining liquidity out of emerging markets and risk assets.
2022-Q3.lesson: During quantitative tightening, cash reserves offer peace of mind and dry powder for bargain hunting.

2022-Q4.headline: Inflation Begins to Cool, Gold Soars (+9.8%)
2022-Q4.context: First CPI readings show softening inflation. Markets sigh in relief and appetite for risk begins to return.
2022-Q4.lesson: The most challenging year in modern memory has concluded. Check if your portfolio preserved purchasing power!

verdicts.sunglasses_and_suit: Terrific job, Boss! You survived this historic storm in style and with strong profits. You proved you understand how markets work!
verdicts.happy: Well done! You finished in the green despite tremendous market turbulence. The most important lesson: markets always recover losses if you give them time.
verdicts.supportive_with_lifejacket: Don't fret over a temporary dip – in the stock market, losses are only real once you sell at the bottom! Learn from this cycle and prepare for the next stage.

takeaways.drawdown-safe: Outstanding capital protection! Your maximum drawdown was only {absDd}%. Thanks to proper diversification, you avoided the panic that grips most investors.
takeaways.drawdown-deep: You experienced a deep capital drawdown ({absDd}%). In equity markets, such pullbacks happen regularly – the key to survival is a long time horizon and a cash cushion.
takeaways.inflation-beat: You beat inflation! Your real return was +{realPct}%. This means your wealth did not just grow numerically, but can genuinely buy more goods.
takeaways.inflation-lost: Inflation eroded your purchasing power. Remember that holding too much cash guarantees a slow but inevitable loss of real value.
takeaways.rebalance-none: Iron discipline: you didn't make a single panic adjustment during the crisis. Historically, avoiding rash moves is one of the most profitable investor traits.
takeaways.rebalance-active: During the cycle, you made {count} adjustments to your portfolio. Conscious rebalancing allows buying discounted assets, but remember not to chase the market based on news headlines.
